name: Structural Biology (PhD)

rules.name: Elective Courses
rules.desc: At least three additional graduate-level courses in physical or biological sciences, with at least one course in physical science and at least one in literature-based biological science.

rules.name: Dissertation Proposal
rules.desc: The student must prepare a dissertation proposal defining the research to be undertaken, including methods of procedure. This proposal should be submitted by the end of summer quarter of the second year, and it must be approved by a committee of at least three members, including the principal research advisor and at least one member from the Department of Structural Biology. The candidate must defend the dissertation proposal in an oral examination. The dissertation reading committee typically evolves from the dissertation proposal review committee.

rules.name: Oral Exam
rules.desc: The student must pass the University Oral Examination, taken only after substantially completing the research. The examination is preceded by a public seminar in which the candidate presents the research.

rules.name: Dissertation
rules.desc: The student must present a PhD dissertation as the result of an independent investigation and express a contribution to knowledge in structural biology.

transferPolicy: The Structural Biology department will allow up to the university limit of 45 units of graduate-level coursework to apply toward department degree requirements.
reviewNotes: You take the five core courses. The three graduate science electives (at least one in physical science and one in literature-based biological science) have no list in the Bulletin, so you move them in by hand, and the dissertation proposal defense, the oral exam and the dissertation are checked by hand.
